cur:objects-coin-basil-ii-constantine-vi.summary: The bust of Christ, with a jewelled cross-nimbus, blesses and holds the Gospels on the obverse; on the reverse the brothers Basil II and Constantine VIII, both crowned, hold a long cross between them. Struck in the early, troubled years of Basil's long reign, the coin continues the tradition of placing the emperors beneath Christ's authority. The broad, flat flan anticipates the later, wider histamenon.
facts: Wikipedia notes that during the later reign of Basil II (976–1025) the histamenon began to be struck thinner and wider, while the lighter tetarteron became smaller and thicker.

feat:duccio-temptation-on-the-mount.summary: Christ, larger than all around him, commands the dark-winged devil to depart, while the kingdoms of the world — tiny walled cities glowing below — lie spread out as the rejected prize. Two angels stand behind him in attendance. The panel once formed part of the back predella of Duccio's Maestà, the monumental altarpiece carried in jubilant procession to Siena Cathedral in 1311.
facts: The Maestà was dismantled in 1771, and its panels were dispersed; several are now in London, Washington, Madrid and New York.
The panel came to the Frick in 1927, purchased with the collection of Robert H. Benson of London through Duveen Brothers.
Duccio renders the 'kingdoms of the world' as tiny, jewel-like walled cities, each carefully detailed, set against the black, winged figure of Satan.
Contemporary chroniclers describe the whole city of Siena closing its shops to escort the finished Maestà to the cathedral.
